papers.title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement in Pure Aortic Regurgitation: The Randomized SEASON-AR Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: In this Chinese open-label trial, 210 patients with severe pure aortic regurgitation who were poor or unwilling surgical candidates were randomised to transfemoral TAVR with the VitaFlow valve plus medical therapy, or medical therapy alone. At 1 year, death, disabling stroke or heart failure rehospitalisation occurred in 8.3% vs 24.8% (HR 0.31, 95% CI 0.14-0.66; P=0.001), driven by fewer heart failure rehospitalisations (3.7% vs 21.3%). TAVR brought more major or life-threatening bleeding and new pacemakers, mostly within 30 days.
papers.short_title: TAVR versus medical therapy for pure aortic regurgitation in SEASON-AR

papers.title: Bivalirudin With a High-Dose Post-PCI Infusion Versus Heparin During Primary PCI in STEMI: One-Year Results From the BRIGHT-4 Trial.
papers.summary: One-year follow-up of 6,016 patients with STEMI having radial primary PCI, randomised to bivalirudin with a 2 to 4 hour high-dose post-PCI infusion or to heparin alone. Death or BARC type 3 to 5 bleeding at 12 months occurred in 4.1% vs 5.6% (HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.58-0.92; P=0.007). Bivalirudin also lowered major bleeding (0.6% vs 1.2%; HR 0.49) and stent thrombosis (0.8% vs 1.3%; P=0.045), while all-cause death was not significantly different (3.8% vs 4.8%; P=0.08).
papers.short_title: one-year results of bivalirudin versus heparin in BRIGHT-4

papers.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Reducing LV Afterload With Impella or Intra-Aortic Balloon Counterpulsation During Veno-Arterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Cardiogenic Shock: HERACLES Trial.
papers.summary: This mechanistic trial randomised 24 patients on VA-ECMO for SCAI stage D or E cardiogenic shock to left ventricular unloading with an intra-aortic balloon pump or a micro-axial flow pump (Impella). The myocardial oxygen supply-demand ratio improved with the balloon pump but not with the micro-axial pump (1.48 vs 0.97; P=0.036), mainly through lower oxygen demand, and coronary flow rose marginally with the balloon pump only. Thirty-day mortality was similar (38% vs 45%).
papers.short_title: Impella versus balloon pump unloading on VA-ECMO in HERACLES

papers.title: Posterior Leaflet Restoration for Secondary Mitral Regurgitation: EXPLORE MR Results.
papers.summary: Early feasibility study of posterior leaflet restoration with the MRace implant, an inflatable coaptation element, in 78 patients with severe secondary mitral regurgitation. The implant was deployed in 96.2%, 30-day mortality was 6.4%, and MR of 2+ or less was achieved in 93.8% at 30 days and 90.6% at 1 year. Results were better without severe LV enlargement: 1-year mortality was 19.4% versus 41.7% in severely enlarged ventricles (29.5% overall).
papers.short_title: posterior leaflet restoration for secondary mitral regurgitation in EXPLORE MR

papers.title: Prognostic Impact of Discharge Transprosthetic Tricuspid Gradient After Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement: The TRIPLACE Registry.
papers.summary: In 474 patients from the international TRIPLACE transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement registry, a discharge transprosthetic gradient of 3.5 mm Hg or more (25.7% of patients) was linked to worse outcomes. After adjustment it remained associated with 3-year mortality (adjusted HR 1.84, 95% CI 1.09-3.10) and with death or heart failure hospitalisation (adjusted HR 1.77). A smaller indexed inner valve diameter was the only modifiable predictor of a high gradient.
papers.short_title: discharge gradient after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement in TRIPLACE

papers.title: Microvascular Resistance Reserve and Outcomes in Angina and Nonobstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
papers.summary: In 553 patients with angina and nonobstructive coronary arteries from a Dutch multicentre registry, 17.0% had coronary microvascular dysfunction by continuous-thermodilution microvascular resistance reserve (below 2.1). Over a mean 27.5 months, the composite clinical outcome did not differ by MRR category (19.1%, 21.4% and 21.1%; P=.85). Low MRR was, however, linked to worse angina at follow-up and less clinically relevant symptom improvement (30.0% vs 59.1%).
papers.short_title: microvascular resistance reserve in angina with nonobstructive coronaries

Intensive vs More Intensive Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Plaque Regression in Statin-Naive Patients: Prespecified Analyses From the FLOWPROMOTE Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: In 104 statin-naive patients with stable coronary disease, rosuvastatin 40 mg plus ezetimibe lowered LDL cholesterol more than atorvastatin 40 mg (to 42.5 vs 69.5 mg/dL). On CT angiography at 18 months, total plaque volume fell 21.1% versus 13.6% (P=.02), with greater noncalcified plaque regression too. Lower achieved LDL tracked with more regression.
papers.study_type: Prespecified analysis of a randomised trial
papers.short_title: more intensive lipid lowering and plaque regression in FLOWPROMOTE

papers.title: N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small Interfering RNA Targeting Hepatic Angiotensinogen in Hypertension: A Phase I Clinical Trial With Randomized Part A and Open-Label Part B.
papers.summary: This phase I trial gave ART101, a liver-targeted RNA drug silencing angiotensinogen, once to 40 healthy volunteers (placebo-controlled) and 8 patients with hypertension. It was well tolerated, without serious adverse events. At 600 mg angiotensinogen fell about 90%, and placebo-corrected 24-hour systolic pressure in healthy participants was 12.9 mm Hg lower at 24 weeks.
papers.short_title: an angiotensinogen-silencing RNA drug for hypertension

papers.title: Intersection of Patient and Hospital Rurality in Heart Failure Care and Outcomes.
papers.summary: Among 735,460 Medicare patients hospitalised for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, rural patients treated in urban rather than rural hospitals more often saw a cardiologist (OR 2.02), started more guideline-directed therapies, and had lower one-year readmission and mortality. Rural patients still had slightly higher 30- and 90-day mortality than urban patients.
papers.short_title: patient and hospital rurality in heart failure care

papers.title: Systemic Hypertension and Survival in Pulmonary Hypertension.
papers.summary: In 12,771 patients with pulmonary hypertension from a global registry, those with preexisting systemic hypertension had 26% lower mortality (HR 0.74), and survival improved with higher systolic systemic pressure across all pulmonary hypertension groups. A higher heart rate and falling systemic pressure during follow-up were linked to higher mortality, confirmed in a UK cohort.
papers.short_title: systemic hypertension and survival in pulmonary hypertension

papers.title: Assessment of Ototoxicity in Patients With Heart Failure Receiving High-Dose IV Loop Diuretics.
papers.summary: Across two small heart failure cohorts given high-dose intravenous loop diuretics (up to 500 mg furosemide), no permanent hearing loss was seen; transient hearing shifts at peak concentration (6% of ears) mostly resolved within hours. In 22,656 hospitalisations, peak doses of 160 mg furosemide equivalents or more were not linked to diagnosed ototoxicity.
papers.short_title: hearing and high-dose loop diuretics in heart failure
